title: runtime: kernel selector v2 core (table-driven) + registry loader + unit tests
author: Grace Kim
description: Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 moves kernel choice from heuristic-only selection to a table-driven registry keyed on request context. This PR lands the core selector v2 interfaces + selection flow (no scheduler wiring yet), plus an initial registry loader and unit tests to lock down determinism and fallback behavior. Goals: (1) deterministic selection given identical inputs, (2) safe fallback to v1 selector when registry entries are missing/invalid, (3) strict validation + clear debug surfaces for later telemetry/explain tooling, and (4) small initial registry stub to prove end-to-end wiring. Implementation summary: Adds SelectorV2 that consumes SelectionContext (model_family, attention_flags, seq_bucket, gpu_sku, sm_capability) and chooses a KernelId via a table-driven lookup with explicit precedence (exact match -> wildcard fallbacks -> safe kernel set -> v1). Introduces KernelRegistry (versioned) with JSON schema validation at load time; registry is loaded at runtime startup and can be reloaded via config push (no hot reload by default; reload is behind an internal toggle and returns errors without swapping if validation fails). Unknown/partial metadata never crashes serving: selector returns "use_v1" + reason and emits an internal debug log (telemetry will be added in a follow-on PR). Determinism: tie-breaking is stable and documented (lexicographic on KernelId after precedence rank). Safety: adds a "safe_set" of baseline kernels per GPU family as a final non-v1 fallback for known-good shapes (kept minimal for now; conformance coverage to be expanded in ENG-3928). Unit tests cover: registry parsing/validation errors, wildcard matching, deterministic tie-breaking, fallback to v1, and handling of missing fields in context. Notes/limitations: This PR does not introduce feature flag wiring, scheduler-provided seq bucket, GPU SKU normalization, or production telemetry. Those land in follow-ups (ENG-3924/3925/3927/3931). This PR is intended to unblock benchmark harness integration and enable iterative registry population without touching the selection code. Testing: unit tests added under runtime/selector/tests; ran runtime_tests and selector_tests in CI; manual local run with a stub registry to verify startup + selection call path. Rollout: none (selector v2 not enabled by default and not wired into request path yet).

runtime/selector: implement table-driven lookup with precedence + deterministic tie-break
runtime/registry: add KernelRegistry schema + JSON loader + validation
runtime/selector: add SafeKernelSet fallback for known GPU families
runtime/selector/tests: add unit tests for matching + fallback + determinism
docs(internal): add developer notes on registry precedence and error handling
changed_areas: runtime/config (plumbing for registry path + basic validation hooks)
snippet: Example selection precedence implemented in selector_v2.cc (simplified): 1) exact match on (model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku) 2) wildcard gpu_sku=* 3) wildcard seq_bucket=* 4) wildcard both 5) safe_set[gpu_family] 6) fallback_to_v1(reason). Tie-break: if multiple candidates within same precedence rank, choose smallest KernelId lexicographically to keep selection stable across map iteration order.
review_conversation: Noah Patel (review): The overall structure looks good. Two asks: (1) document the precedence order in code comments and (2) make sure tie-break doesn’t depend on container iteration order. Also please add a unit test that ensures repeated calls with same context give same KernelId even if registry map insertion order differs.

Grace Kim (author): Added explicit precedence comment block in selector_v2.cc and switched candidate collection to a vector sorted by (precedence_rank, kernel_id). Added test case that loads the same entries in different order and asserts identical selection.

Yuki Sato (review): For GPU field naming, you used gpu_sku and sm_capability in context. We’ll normalize SKUs later (ENG-3925), but can we ensure selector behavior is sane if gpu_sku is empty? Right now it looks like we’ll go to wildcard entries; that’s fine but please ensure empty string is treated as unknown and not as a valid exact-match value.

Grace Kim (author): Good catch. Updated matcher: empty gpu_sku is treated as unknown and bypasses exact-match on sku; it can match wildcard gpu_sku='*' and then safe_set. Added tests for empty gpu_sku and missing sm_capability.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Registry loader currently returns Status::InvalidArgument with a single string. For debugging, can we include a list of validation errors (field path + message) so later we can surface in config validation logs? Doesn’t need to be a structured type yet, but at least join multiple issues.

Grace Kim (author): Implemented aggregation in registry validator: collects (json_pointer, message) and joins into one string separated by '\n'. Added fixture with multiple errors and asserts message contains both pointers.

Thomas Baird (review): Please be careful with logging. I see debug logs printing full model name and registry path. For future telemetry cardinality, we should avoid per-request logs. This PR isn’t on the hot path yet but please add a TODO and ensure logs are only on registry load errors and not per selection call.

Grace Kim (author): Removed per-call debug logs; selector returns a reason string to the caller but doesn’t log. Loader logs only on load/validation errors at startup. Added TODO for ENG-3927 about emitting structured telemetry with bucketing.
Noah Patel (final review): Looks good. Approved once CI is green.
CI (bot): selector-tests failed: flaky ordering assumption in SelectorV2DeterminismTest
Grace Kim (author): Fixed test to shuffle insertion order deterministically via seeded RNG and compare results across two differently ordered registries; re-ran CI.
